articles.title: Virgil van Dijk warns Manchester City players to get used to hostile atmospheres
articles.summary: Liverpool captain says players heard ‘cheat’ chants. ‘I don’t think Anfield will be the only place’ Virgil van Dijk has suggested Manchester City’s treatment at the hands of the Liverpool crowd on Sunday was a sign of things to come and something their players will have to get used to.
body: City were barracked throughout the game at Anfield, their first since they were found guilty of almost all the charges they faced in relation to breaking the Premier League’s financial rules between 2009 and 2018. An independent commission declared that City had overstated their income by £830.69m and would have been in breach of spending regulations in the Premier League and Europe if they had provided a true picture of their finances.

The Anfield crowd denounced City as cheats in various chants and Van Dijk said it was impossible for the players not to hear them. City were unaffected, running out 3-0 winners after the game turned on the 62nd-minute dismissal of the Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch.

“I think everyone could hear it,” Van Dijk said. “Everyone can share their feelings and I don’t think Anfield will be the only place where it will be the case because fans will have their feelings. But for players I don’t think it is a good idea at this moment in time [to share their feelings].”

articles.title: Women's billion-dollar boom leaves players behind, says Fifpro
articles.summary: Women's football is on course to become a billion-dollar industry, but many professional players are still earning low wages, working on insecure contracts and experiencing rising psychological stress, a Fifpro survey indicates.
body: Players were asked why they might leave football early. The report stated 59% cited financial reasons, while psychological stress was another factor identified by 46%.

Alex Culvin, head of women's football at Fifpro, said there was no single explanation for the increase. She pointed to growing public exposure, financial insecurity and inadequate support systems as possible contributing factors.
"Players are not only expected to be visible, but are obligated to be visible because of the low income to subsidise the lack of solid income they receive."
While awareness of mental health issues has improved, Culvin explained many players felt they were being left to cope alone.

articles.title: The Hotspot | Alexéi Rojas: ‘I’m passionate about sustainability – I told Arsenal: we need to fix this’
articles.summary: The 21-year-old goalkeeper wants to impress on football the need to change old habits for the sake of the planet. “I’m a bit of an outlier as a person, I like being unique in who I am and what I do,” says the former Arsenal goalkeeper Alexéi Rojas, who combines saving shots with saving the planet.
body: There is plenty to make him stand out. By 15, Rojas was changing the way people thought at Arsenal, transforming attitudes at the academy’s Hale End training ground where he would cycle, rather than get a lift from his parents. Rojas’s interest in the climate crisis began thanks to his mother, who works in wind energy. He would visit her office to learn more about renewables and their potential.

“I spoke about sustainability in front of everyone [at the academy],” Rojas says. “The staff realised this is something I’m really passionate about. I jumped at the opportunity. I said: ‘We need to fix this.’

“First, there’s no recycling bins, we need to incorporate that. We use way too much plastic, which we can swap out for reusable things or compostable packaging; there’s a lot of energy wasted at the training ground where there’s lights on all the time that don’t need to be.”
This transformation led to more interest from teammates, who quickly switched to reusable bottles, a small indication of what can happen when someone makes a stand.
points: The 21-year-old goalkeeper wants to impress on football the need to change old habits for the sake of the planet.

articles.title: The Browns are still the Browns. And Deshaun Watson is still Deshaun Watson
articles.summary: After three straight game-winning drives, Cleveland’s quarterback was sacked eight times in a dismal defeat that punctured the hype surrounding his revival. I guess the New York Jets didn’t get the memo. This was supposed to be a Deshaun Watson lovefest.
body: Limping along for 155 passing yards and one touchdown, Watson fell to Earth harder than David Bowie in a Nicolas Roeg film (yes, I just watched the Dennis Miller Monday Night Football documentary on HBO). He completed fewer than 50% of his passes and ended the day with a 69.6 passer rating. I should also probably mention he got sacked eight times. Yes, eight times. EIGHT TIMES. He only completed seven more passes than he received punishing hits behind the line of scrimmage. It was a performance NBC NFL writer Patrick Daugherty called “ unspeakably bad.” Actually, I think the performance was very much speakable, as I’ve demonstrated here. Stick around for another 400 words.

The thing that has defined Watson’s run as a potentially viable NFL quarterback has been his ability to march down the field and win a game in the dying embers of the contest. After three game-winning drives to start the season, it seemed like the Browns were poised to pull out another improbable victory from deep where the sun don’t shine, but no. Not today.

articles.title: Seedorf back in football as Corinthians head coach
articles.summary: Brazilian club Corinthians appoint Clarence Seedorf as their head coach, with the former Netherlands midfielder taking on his first coaching role since 2019.
body: The 50-year-old has joined on a contract until the end of 2027 with the club 16th in the Brazilian top flight, one place above the relegation zone with eight games left.
Seedorf succeeds former Brazil interim national coach Fernando Diniz, who was sacked by Corinthians last week after the club lost seven consecutive league games.
Seedorf's last coaching role was with the Cameroon national team more than seven years ago, while he has previously had underwhelming spells at AC Milan, Shenzhen FC and Deportivo La Coruna.

"Taking on this challenge is an honour, but also a huge responsibility. I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory," said Seedorf of his Corinthians appointment.

articles.summary: Nick Sirianni is getting heat for having Philadelphia in a unfamiliar place below.500 with Jalen Hurts and the offense struggling. Here's why every Eagles fan just need to relax about a tough start.

The Eagles are in an unfamiliar position under.500 in Nick Sirianni coaching era. Philadelphia, after an apt franchise record of having a winning record through 76 consecutive games, fell to 2-3 after the team's frustrating 19-17 loss to Jacksonville in London on Sunday.

The Eagles, going into Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season, are experiencing a sub-..500 feeling for the first time since Week 15 of 2021, the first season of Sirianni's tenure. That year, the Eagles went from 6-7 to finish 9-8 to earn a NFC wild-card berth.

In the previous five seasons under Sirianni, the Eagles made the playoffs in each, with three NFC East division titles and a ring from Super Bowl 59. Even with Sirianni blaming himself for the loss to the Jaguars, his regular-season winning percentage remains.678 (61-29) through 90 games.

articles.title: Virgil van Dijk’s says views on ‘great rivalry’ with Man City have not changed despite guilty verdict
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk insisted that Liverpool had enjoyed a great rivalry against Manchester City and that his feelings about it have not changed after their rivals were found guilty of 114 charges of breaching Premier League financial rules.
body: City were deemed to have inflated their income by more than £900m in a nine-year period, giving them a spending power which helped them twice pip Liverpool to the title by one point.

But Van Dijk, who was part of a Liverpool side who displaced Pep Guardiola’s side as champions in 2020 and who knocked them out of the Champions League in 2018, said the damning verdict on City and their era of dominance has not altered his own thoughts about their battles.
“No, because I really enjoyed our rivalry and it was a great rivalry on the pitch,” he said. “What happened off the pitch that is for others to find a conclusion on and then let’s see.”
City are appealing against the verdict and while Van Dijk believes it would not be clever for him to discuss it now, he hinted he will when there is some finality to the situation.

body: Minutes after confirming Ramis’s departure, Osasuna officially announced an agreement with Jagoba Arrasate to take charge of the team. The Biscay-born coach returns to his former club on a long-term contract that will keep him there until June 30, 2029.

Arrasate’s return underlines the board’s firm commitment to a stable sporting project that the El Sadar faithful can fully trust. During his previous spell, the coach oversaw one of the club’s most consistent periods in the top flight.

The coach will lead his first training session with the squad at the Tajonar facilities to begin preparations for the next league fixture. His official presentation to the media will take place in the coming hours in the stadium’s press room.

articles.title: Neville and Carra: ‘Stain’ hangs over Man City until financial charges resolved
articles.summary: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have warned that a ‘stain’ will continue to hang over Manchester City and the Premier League until the club’s financial charges are finally resolved.
body: City's victory at Liverpool on Sunday, which hinged on Ryan Gravenberch's controversial dismissal, took them back to the top of the Premier League.

But the win was inevitably overshadowed after the independent Premier League commission found Manchester City in breach of the Premier League's financial rules - City have denied wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal - with Sky Sports commentator Peter Drury describing the game as "the most peculiar day in Premier League history".

"We're sat here not knowing what it means," reflected Gary Neville. "City supporters will be delighted [with the win], but I don't think they recognise right now the stain, the stigma and the damage this is going to do to them.
"Liverpool fans are singing 'going down', they're shouting 'cheats' and you can't get away from that."
